headline: Washington, D.C.'s likely next mayor, Janeese Lewis George, has said it would be irresponsible to rush a council bill that would allow robotaxis such as Waymo, because of the risk to workers' jobs.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a local lawmaking fight over robotaxis in the US capital, but the vote date is not confirmed and the statement dates from 15 Oct 2026.
importance_line: Rideshare and taxi drivers, riders and the council are affected, and the opposition of the likely next mayor could slow the bill, but it is unclear when any vote will happen because Axios' headline says it is set while City Cast DC found no public date.
summary: City Cast DC reports that Janeese Lewis George, a Ward 4 councilmember and the Democratic nominee for mayor, said on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 that rushing the legalization of autonomous vehicles is "irresponsible" given expected AI-related job losses, while the D.C. Council has been reviewing a bill since May that would allow robotaxis such as Alphabet's Waymo. Labor unions oppose the bill, and City Cast DC says Waymo has worked with Councilmember Charles Allen to add a fund for workers who lose jobs.
notes: Kept the pool default ROB; the robotaxi bill could also be read as LAW. Axios, the pool source, is blocked; story read at City Cast DC and Gadget Review. Conflict on timing: Axios headline "set for council vote" (16 Oct 2026) versus City Cast DC "no public date" (15 Oct 2026); not resolved. Waymo's role in the fund comes from City Cast DC's text, not a Waymo statement. Policy item: no machine operating.
